title: Prometheus-alpha v0.3: memory surgery, a sparse compiler, an engram decoder, balanced selection and fission
status: Locked before any v0.3 experiment on a confirmatory rule. B0 and B1 were training (from S0 and S1) when this was locked. v0.1 and v0.2 locks unchanged.
code: src/prometheus/v3.py and train_v3.py (the v0.1 and v0.2 code is imported unchanged)

rules.B0, B1: each initialised from S0 / S1 and trained 1,500 iterations on lives with two successive amputations after conditioning (head 70%, tail 15%, none 15% each), memory scored after both regrowths; batch 32, Adam 2e-3 with the v0.1 schedule

H14.claim: Memory surgery: the rule's v0.2 compiled pattern for the other odour, written into a trained worm's decapitated body, overwrites its memory in the regrown head
H14.measure: overwrite = ((pref_A-trained without - with) + (pref_B-trained with - without)) / 4 per worm index; 1 = a full switch

H15.claim: Sparse compiler: a pattern designed only at sites 12-15 (design seed 4150, 32 worms, 150 Adam steps) writes a memory into held-out untrained decapitated bodies
H15.measure: (pref with A pattern - pref with B pattern) / 2 per held-out worm (seed 4151)

H16.claim: Engram decoder: a ridge readout of the odour from one cell's 10 hidden channels, fit on half the decapitated paired worms at sites up to 15, identifies the odour better from the edge cells (12-15) than from the rest of the trunk (16-27) in the other half
H16.measure: correct(edge majority) - correct(rest majority) per held-out worm

H17.claim: Balanced selection: at cycle 4, a B rule remembers its S sibling's disfavoured odour better than the S sibling does
H17.measure: M(B) - M(S) for the same worms of the disfavoured odour (S0: A, S1: B), seed 4017
H17.rules: tested in the S0/S1 runs against B0/B1

H18.claim: Fission: after cutting a trained worm at site 20 and 48 steps of regrowth, the posterior half (which must regrow a head) remembers
H18.measure: M of the posterior half, per worm (twins cut the same way)
H18.secondary: memory of the anterior half, which keeps the head

decision_rules.family: H14-H18 per rule (H17 in S rules); Holm at alpha 0.05; SESOI 0.10; replicated = supported in both rules of a family

predictions.H14: S rules: supported. E rules: no prediction (their bodies hold no memory to overwrite; the v0.2 compiler wrote one odour only)
predictions.H15: S rules: supported (v0.2: the memory lives at these sites). E rules: not supported
predictions.H16: S rules: supported. E rules: not supported
predictions.H17: supported in both, by a small margin
predictions.H18: S rules: NOT supported, the posterior half forgets while the anterior half remembers. E rules: not supported

disclosed_pilots: No v0.3 pilots were run on pilot rules for H14, H15 or H17. A code smoke test of H16 and H18 on pilot rule S102 at n = 16 was seen before the lock: decoder edge accuracy 0.88 vs rest 0.38; fission posterior half -0.01, anterior half 0.91. It informed the H16 and H18 predictions.
